slides.title: One agentic system, end to end

elements.text: One agentic system, end to end
The course takes one agentic system and walks it from the agent loop down to the serving stack and the hardware under it.
A request that has to be finished, not merely answered.
Plan, act, observe, adapt, deliver. Context, memory, tools, subagents.
Batching, scheduling, routing, caching. Inference is the cost center.
CUDA, Triton, collectives, and the machines underneath.

Agent design: context, memory, tools, evaluation
Serving: batching, scheduling, caching, routing
Multi-agent coordination and communication
Cost, performance and safety of the whole stack

Training: pre-training, fine-tuning, post-training, RL rollout
Data pipeline and checkpointing
Cluster management; model architecture design
Communication, power and energy; new hardware design

slides.title: Five Mads assignments, 70% of the grade

elements.text: Five Mads assignments, 70% of the grade

Mads abbreviates Modern Agent Design and Systems, and nods to Harvard's MaDSys group. Only Assignments 1 to 3 have published full specifications; for Assignments 4 and 5 the index page publishes date, weight, codename, one-paragraph summary and effort estimate only.
The policy page says every assignment submits three artifacts; the index disagrees about A3 and A5 - see the briefing deck.

slides.title: The arc walks down the stack

elements.text: The arc walks down the stack
Use the agent. Build a web UI that drives Claude Code.
Replace the runtime with your own agent loop.
Optimize everything around a black-box API.
Remove the API and own the serving engine.
The grading instrument changes with the assignment: feature checklist (A1), hidden held-out tasks (A2), leaderboard rank (A3). Each step removes more of the scaffolding the course provides.
No exam, no midterm and no final. Lectures are not recorded.

The published breakdown disagrees with itself. This slide follows the course site policy page. Lecture 1's grading slide (2026-09-02) lists a different split: assignments 1, 2 and 4 at 10% each, assignments 3 and 5 at 20% each, project 16%, presentation 10%, participation 4%, bonus 10%. The two published sets are not reconciled in the course materials.

slides.title: The final project: one claim, measured

elements.text: The final project: one claim, measured
Individual, 20% of the course grade. One proposal, one poster and demo, one blog post and repository.

Build an AI system that solves a real problem better than the strongest available alternative
The gap may come from missing context, poor reliability, high cost, slow response, privacy constraints, or an unsupported workflow
Run at least three of the closest commercial tools, open-source systems or research prototypes, and give the same input directly to a frontier model

Make an original, falsifiable claim about agents or the systems that run them
Establish a result the closest published work does not provide, explain why it occurs, and define the conditions under which it holds
A polished implementation, reproduction, benchmark or set of measurements does not meet the bar alone

slides.title: The rules that shape the work

elements.text: The rules that shape the work

Four for the semester, in whole days, spendable across assignments
A submission one minute late consumes a full day
After that, late work loses 20% of its value per day, to a floor of zero after five days

AI use is encouraged and never replaces authorship
Every submitted artifact must describe which tools were used and for what
Undisclosed AI use is an integrity violation

No more than 20% of the class receives an A
There is no midterm and no final, and lectures are not recorded
Auditing is allowed if there is room, but auditors are not graded

10% of the grade for active participation
Attendance is not tracked, so no participation means a participation score of zero
Bonus is capped at 10% overall: optional presentations, course feedback, and problems current AI cannot solve
FIVE RULES FOR READING THESE DECKS

One lecture deck per published lecture PDF. Each deck mirrors a single deck from the course slides directory.
Every slide carries a provenance footer naming the upstream artifact, so any claim can be traced back to its source.
Many figures in the source decks are images with no extractable text. These decks reproduce the text, numbers and tables, and they do not redraw the original diagrams.

slides.title: Five things to carry out of this course

elements.text: Five things to carry out of this course
This is a systems course: the object of study is the whole agentic serving system, not the model.
Capability becomes product only through systems work, and that work is harder than the AI itself.
Optimize task success per dollar and per unit of energy, not tokens per second.
The assignments walk down the stack: use, build, optimize, serve, then optimize the whole stack.
Every agentic workload property is a systems problem, and the workload table is effectively the syllabus.
